title: Bulgaria says a five-year hacking operation downloaded 62 million pages of government documents
date_note: Reuters' dateline is 18 November (the ministry spoke on Wednesday); the pages give no exact day for when the intrusion began beyond 2021 or for the August detection.
org: Government of Bulgaria (Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation)
geo_basis: national government and the ministry that made the announcement; Sofia is the capital
summary: Bulgaria's Innovation and Digital Transformation Minister Ivan Vassilev said, per Reuters, that since 2021 more than 130 GB, or 62 million pages, of documents had been downloaded in a hacking operation. A new national monitoring system detected suspicious activity in August. The ministry said there was no evidence so far that personal data was compromised and no conclusive evidence linking the attackers to a foreign government.
plain: Bulgaria's government says hackers took government documents for years. The ministry says it found no evidence so far that people's personal data was taken.
exec: A national government says a long-running intrusion downloaded 62 million pages of documents, a reminder that undetected access can last years.

evidence.quote: since 2021 more than 130 GB, or 62 million pages, of documents had been downloaded
there was no evidence so far that Bulgarians' personal data had been compromised
the hackers downloaded at least 130 gigabytes of documents, equivalent to more than 62 million pages.

key_findings: Ministry says documents were downloaded since 2021; detected in August by a new national monitoring system
Several international hacking groups believed behind it; no conclusive evidence of a foreign government or intelligence service
Affected systems isolated, access cut off, malware removed; prosecutors notified

validation.note: Reuters (via The Star) and Anadolu (via ANews) both relay the ministry's statement of the 62 million pages; the ministry's own page was not read. Wording differs (Reuters: more than 130 GB, or 62 million pages; Anadolu: at least 130 gigabytes, more than 62 million pages).
